answer: New identities enter through one narrow wharf, not the open ocean: each may take only tiny jobs at first, and its signal of trust rises solely from independently verified completions, never from self-declared claims. Trust cannot be transferred or pooled between identities, and it decays without fresh work. An attacker spinning up thousands of fakes therefore pays the full cost, real checked work and waiting time, for every single identity, while still stuck at the lowest tier where valuable jobs are out of reach.
